questions.q: In our field coordinates, where is (0, 0)?
questions.correct: The center of the field
wrong: The red drivers' corner
Wherever the robot starts
The middle of the red hive
questions.explain: Field coordinates put (0, 0) at the field center, so everyone agrees where everything is. The robot's start spot is NOT (0, 0) anymore.

questions.q: Seen from the red drivers, which way does +Y point?
questions.correct: Away from the drivers
wrong: Toward the drivers
To the drivers' right
To the drivers' left
questions.explain: +X is to the drivers' right, and +Y is away from them, toward the far wall, just like graph paper.

questions.q: Which direction is 0° on the field?
questions.correct: Along +X, to the drivers' right
wrong: Along +Y, away from the drivers
Toward the red drivers
Wherever the robot faces
questions.explain: Angles start at +X and grow counter-clockwise: 90° is away from the drivers, 180° is left, −90° is toward them.

questions.q: Which way do angles grow (get bigger) on the field?
questions.correct: Counter-clockwise
wrong: Clockwise
Toward the hive
Toward the drivers
questions.explain: Counter-clockwise is +. That's the math convention, so Java's Math functions agree with us.

questions.q: A turret angle of +30° means the turret points...
questions.correct: 30° to the left of the front
wrong: 30° to the right of the front
30° away from the drivers
30° above the floor
questions.explain: + is counter-clockwise, which is to the left. Negative turret angles point right.

questions.q: The robot is at (0, −32.4) and the cell is at (10.2, −12.75). What is dx?
questions.explain: dx = targetX − robotX = 10.2 − 0 = 10.2. It's how far OVER the target is.

questions.q: The robot is at (0, −32.4) and the cell is at (10.2, −12.75). What is dy?
questions.explain: dy = targetY − robotY = −12.75 − (−32.4) = 19.65. Subtracting a negative is adding.

questions.q: What question does Math.atan2(dy, dx) answer?
questions.correct: Which direction does the arrow point?
wrong: How long is the arrow?
How fast should the turret turn?
Where is the robot on the field?
questions.explain: atan2 takes 'how far up' and 'how far over' and gives the arrow's direction. (Math.hypot gives the length.)

questions.q: Why atan2 instead of a math function that takes just one number?
questions.correct: It uses both signs, so it knows all four directions
wrong: It is faster for the Control Hub to calculate
It returns degrees instead of radians
It works only for targets in front of the robot
questions.explain: The '2' means two inputs. With both signs, atan2 can tell up-right from down-left, and gives −180° to 180°.

questions.q: Math.atan2 gives its answer in radians. How do we get degrees?
questions.correct: Wrap it in Math.toDegrees()
wrong: Multiply it by 360
Wrap it in Math.abs()
Divide it by Math.PI
questions.explain: Math.toDegrees(Math.atan2(dy, dx)) gives the direction in degrees.

questions.q: What is the auto-aim formula (before trim)?
questions.correct: turret angle = field angle − robot heading
wrong: turret angle = field angle + robot heading
turret angle = robot heading − field angle
turret angle = field angle × robot heading
questions.explain: The field angle is measured from +X; the turret measures from the robot's front. Subtracting the heading converts one to the other.

questions.q: The cell is at a field angle of 63°. The robot's heading is 90°. What turret angle aims at it?
questions.correct: −27° (27° to the right)
wrong: +27° (27° to the left)
+153° (behind on the left)
+63° (63° to the left)
questions.explain: 63 − 90 = −27. Negative means clockwise, which is to the right.

questions.q: The robot spins in place but doesn't move. What happens to the field angle to the cell?
questions.correct: It stays the same
wrong: It changes by the same amount
It flips to the other side
It resets to zero
questions.explain: The field angle only depends on where the robot and cell ARE. Spinning changes the heading, so only the turret angle changes.

questions.q: The subtraction gives 340°. What turret angle should we send?
questions.explain: 340° and −20° point the same way. Wrapping: more than 180, so subtract 360 → −20°. A short turn right instead of a long turn left.

questions.q: Why can our turret point in ANY direction, even straight behind the robot?
questions.correct: It turns about 407°, more than a full circle
wrong: Its servo is in continuous mode, so it spins forever
The Pinpoint turns the turret around when needed
The wires are attached to a spinning slip ring
questions.explain: 350° × 3.2 ÷ 2.75 ≈ 407° across the servo's full 500–2500 µs signal. We allow ±200°, which covers every direction.

questions.q: What does servo.setPwmRange(new PwmControl.PwmRange(500, 2500)) do?
questions.correct: Asks for the servo's full signal range
wrong: Makes the servo spin 500 to 2500 times faster
Limits the turret to a safe range of motion
Switches the servo into continuous rotation mode
questions.explain: The hub's default 600–2400 µs only reaches about 90% of the travel (367°). The full 500–2500 µs gives about 407°.

questions.q: The turret is at +185°. The answer is −175°, so the other way is +185°. Which does auto-aim use?
questions.correct: +185°, the shorter swing from where it is
wrong: −175°, because it's between −180 and 180
0°, it goes back to center first
Neither, it waits for the driver
questions.explain: Both point the same way. +185° is 0° away from where the turret is now; −175° would be a 360° swing. Pick the shorter one.

questions.q: Why does auto-aim allow ±200° instead of just ±180°?
questions.correct: The overlap stops flips when the cell wobbles behind
wrong: Because 200 is easier to type than 180
So the trim has more room on the sides
Because the servo is more accurate past 180°
questions.explain: With exactly ±180°, a cell wobbling straight behind would jump between +180 and −180, swinging the turret all the way around. The extra 20° each way gives room to keep going.

questions.q: The driver keeps spinning the robot the same direction. What eventually happens to the turret?
questions.correct: At 200° it unwinds all the way around to the other side
wrong: It keeps turning forever in the same direction
It stops and the cell can't be reached any more
It breaks the wires, so the code shuts it off
questions.explain: Past 200° there's only one way left, so the turret swings around (like untwisting a phone cord) and keeps aiming from the other side.

questions.q: Before letting a real turret swing ±200°, what must you check?
questions.correct: The cables can twist 400° without snagging
wrong: The battery is charged above 13 volts
The Pinpoint is mounted on the turret
The flywheel is spinning at full speed
questions.explain: ±200° twists the shooter's cables through 400°. Give them a service loop or cable carrier, and test slowly with setAngle(±180) first.

questions.q: Why does auto-aim use a trim instead of lesson 17's D-pad nudge?
questions.correct: Auto-aim sets the turret every loop, wiping out a nudge
wrong: The D-pad is broken on most gamepads
A nudge moves the turret much too far
Trim is the only way to move a servo
questions.explain: The trim is an offset added to auto-aim's answer, so it lasts. A nudge would be overwritten on the very next loop.

questions.q: Why is the trim limited to ±20°?
questions.correct: So a bumped stick can't send the aim somewhere silly
wrong: Because the servo can only turn 20°
Because FTC rules limit turret movement
So the flywheel speed stays the same
questions.explain: Trim is for small fixes (a slipped wheel, a cell an inch off). A limit keeps it from wandering far away.

questions.q: How does auto-aim choose which cell to aim at?
questions.correct: The cell on the same side of the field as the robot
wrong: Whichever cell is raised, using the hive's tip sensor
The driver picks it each time with the D-pad
Always the right cell, for the whole match
questions.explain: Left of the middle line (x negative) aims at the left cell; right of it aims at the right cell. The driver decides whether to shoot.

questions.q: The robot is at x = +3, inside the dead zone, and was aiming at the left cell. What does it aim at now?
questions.correct: Still the left cell
wrong: The right cell
Nothing until it leaves the zone
Halfway between the two
questions.explain: Inside the dead zone nothing changes. It only switches to the right cell once x is more than +6.

questions.q: Why have a dead zone in the middle of the field at all?
questions.correct: So the turret doesn't flip between cells on the line
wrong: So the robot can't drive under the hive by accident
Because odometry stops working near the center
Because shots from the middle never go in
questions.explain: Right on the line, a tiny wobble in x would flip the target back and forth. The dead zone means you must clearly cross before it switches.

questions.q: Why does TeleOp call setPose() at all?
questions.correct: So odometry reports real field positions
wrong: So the turret centers itself
So the IMU calibrates its gyro
So the hive knows which cell is up
questions.explain: The Pinpoint zeroes itself at INIT. setPose tells it where it really is, so its numbers match the field and the cell positions.

questions.q: Why call setPose() right after START instead of during INIT?
questions.correct: The Pinpoint calibrates after INIT and could erase it
wrong: The robot isn't allowed to know its pose before START
setPose() only works while the robot is driving
Telemetry can't show the pose until START
questions.explain: The Pinpoint spends a moment calibrating after its reset in INIT. Sending the pose after START makes sure it sticks.

questions.q: Auto just ended. How does TeleOp find out where the robot is?
questions.correct: Auto left its position on the blackboard
wrong: The Pinpoint keeps it, even through INIT
TeleOp assumes it's still at the start spot
The drivers type it into the Driver Station
questions.explain: The blackboard survives from one OpMode to the next. Auto writes its position every loop; TeleOp reads it right after START and calls setPose.

questions.q: Why does auto write its position every loop, not just at the end?
questions.correct: The match timer can stop auto partway through
wrong: The blackboard forgets anything older than one loop
TeleOp reads it while auto is still running
Writing it only once would wear out the Pinpoint
questions.explain: If time runs out mid-path, the code at the end of auto never runs. Saving every loop means the note is always up to date.

questions.q: TeleOp starts and nobody has told it where the robot is. What does the turret do?
questions.correct: Points straight forward and waits
wrong: Aims at the cell from the starting spot
Spins slowly, searching for the hive
Keeps aiming wherever auto last pointed it
questions.explain: Don't guess! A wrong guess would aim confidently at nothing. The turret faces forward until auto's note or a HOME reset tells it where it is.

questions.q: What does holding RB for half a second at HOME do?
questions.correct: Resets field-centric forward AND the robot's position
wrong: Only resets which way is forward for driving
Spins up the flywheel and fires one shot
Saves the position for the next match
questions.explain: At HOME the robot faces away from the drivers at a known spot, so one button can reset the IMU and tell the Pinpoint it's at HOME.

questions.q: Why do you have to HOLD RB instead of just tapping it?
questions.correct: So a bumped button can't move the robot's position
wrong: The IMU needs half a second to wake up
Tapping RB is already used to shoot
The Pinpoint only listens every half second
questions.explain: A quick accidental bump mid-match would tell the robot it's at HOME when it isn't. Requiring a half-second hold makes it deliberate.

questions.q: A driver holds RB in the middle of the field. What goes wrong?
questions.correct: The robot thinks it's at HOME, so shots miss
wrong: Nothing, RB works anywhere on the field
The turret unwinds all the way around
Field-centric driving turns off for good
questions.explain: RB says 'I'm at HOME right now.' Press it anywhere else and odometry jumps to the wrong spot until a proper reset at HOME.

questions.q: What does wrapDegrees() turn 700° into?
questions.explain: The while loop keeps subtracting 360 while the angle is over 180: 700 → 340 → −20.

questions.q: Why does wrapDegrees() use while instead of if?
questions.correct: One subtraction of 360 might not be enough
wrong: A while loop runs faster than an if
An if can't subtract numbers in Java
It only needs to run when the robot moves
questions.explain: A while loop repeats until the angle is in range. 700° needs two trips around; an if would stop after one, at 340°.

questions.q: double targetX = aimingRight ? RIGHT_CELL_X : LEFT_CELL_X; — what if aimingRight is false?
questions.correct: targetX gets LEFT_CELL_X
wrong: targetX gets RIGHT_CELL_X
The line is skipped entirely
targetX is set to zero
questions.explain: question ? ifYes : ifNo is a one-line if/else. aimingRight is false, so it gives back the value after the colon.

questions.q: In the two-ways rule, what does Math.abs(otherWay - now) measure?
questions.correct: How far the turret would swing
wrong: Where the turret is pointing now
How far away the hive is
Which cell the robot is aiming at
questions.explain: otherWay - now is the change in angle, and Math.abs drops the sign. So it's how big the swing is, in either direction.
